trial_court_outcome: Convicted and sentenced to life imprisonment and fined Rs.2000/-
neutral_facts: The accused, a woman, gave birth to a female infant at a hospital. The infant was placed in an incubator with an oxygen mask and did not open her eyes or cry after birth. The infant was handed over to the accused at 04:30 p.m. and found dead by hospital staff at 06:30 p.m. A post-mortem report indicated the cause of death was asphyxia due to ante-mortem strangulation. The prosecution relied on circumstantial evidence, including the testimony of hospital staff and the accused's husband, to establish the accused's guilt. The accused claimed she was not responsible and that the infant's death could have been due to natural causes. The trial court and High Court convicted the accused based on the circumstantial evidence, but the Supreme Court found the evidence insufficient to prove guilt beyond reasonable doubt.
